items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I had been recording with Lou

ctx.x: And I naturally said yes, but I took it with a grain of salt because somebody's always saying, "Well, we're gonna do this and we're gonna do that". However, we were rehearsing at Lou St. 's house, and the nucleus was that ank Lawson and Bob Haggart, naturally, and they were at a loss for a piano player, and we went over to Lou Stein's house -- somebody suggested Lou, I did for one. He was a great player; I had been recording with Lou, and they didn't know if his style would fit in the group of what they had in…
Well, it did. And if you're acquainted with any of the great albums Lou made, God only knows I don't know who would have covered the situation any better.
We had on trombone at the time Cutty Cutshall, and I've got to research this for a moment. That's right, it was Cutty, and Bill Stegmeyer on clarinet, who I wasn't that ...
